You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/reporting-builder (dev merged; reporting dashboards 13.1 done; ALL business modules complete). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL — run the full pg suite). This is the FINAL Phase 13 task; it completes reporting.

Scope per the build spec 13.2: "Generic report builder: entity + columns + filters + group-by → JSON for the grid + CSV export." Plus PERFORMANCE §3: "the report builder caps result rows (10k) and offers CSV export for anything larger, generated by streaming."

READ FIRST (binding): the build spec 13.2; docs/architecture.md D-014 (error envelope, pagination), D-007 (TENANCY — the report builder runs ORM queries that MUST be tenant-filtered; since it queries whitelisted ORM models through the tenant-filtered session, the do_orm_execute listener auto-scopes them — VERIFY this works for the builder's dynamic selects), D-009 (RBAC — a reportable entity is gated by the source module's read permission; and MASKED fields like HR compensation must NOT be exposable through the report builder — exclude masked/sensitive columns from the whitelist), PERFORMANCE §3 (10k row cap + CSV streaming export), §1/§2 (the builder's filters/group-by must hit indexed columns where possible; bound the result). Then read:
- backend/app/modules/reporting/ (the module you extend: constants.py, schemas.py, service.py, router.py, __init__.py).
- backend/app/core/{pagination.py, schemas.py (error envelope), deps.py, models.py}, and how the tenant filter (core/tenancy.py do_orm_execute) applies to ORM selects — the builder MUST go through the ORM (not raw SQL) so tenancy auto-applies; confirm.
- A few module models to whitelist as reportable entities (e.g. finance JournalLine/Account, inventory Item/StockMove, sales SalesOrder, procurement PurchaseOrder, hr Employee — but EXCLUDE Employee's masked compensation columns; pick a SAFE initial whitelist across modules).
- backend/tests/modules/reporting/ (the 13.1 test pattern + cross-module factories).
Latest migration = 0042 (13.2 likely needs NO migration unless you persist saved report definitions — the spec says "report builder" producing JSON+CSV, NOT necessarily saved reports; implement the AD-HOC builder (define-and-run in one request) with NO persistence; if you want saved report defs, that's optional — prefer ad-hoc-only for v1, document; so NO migration).

CRITICAL SECURITY + §5: the report builder must NOT allow querying arbitrary tables/columns (SQL-injection / data-exfiltration risk). It uses a WHITELIST: a registry of reportable entities, each declaring its ORM model + the allowed columns (label, type, filterable, groupable) + the source-module read permission. A report request names a whitelisted entity + a subset of its allowed columns + filters (column from the whitelist + operator from a fixed set + value) + group-by (whitelisted groupable columns) + optional aggregations (count/sum/avg on whitelisted numeric columns). The builder constructs the query via the ORM over the model (so the tenant filter auto-applies via do_orm_execute), NEVER string-concatenated SQL. Reporting imports the whitelisted models — this is a read-only registry; document that this is a sanctioned exception (reporting needs the model classes to build queries; it does NOT call their services). Note in DECISIONS that the report registry importing models is the one place reporting touches models (read-only query construction); confirm no cycle (no module imports reporting).

TASK — PLAN 13.2: generic report builder. Build:

1. reporting/constants.py additions: permission reporting.report.run (or reuse reporting.dashboard.read + per-entity source perms — DECIDE: a base reporting.report.run + each entity gated by its source-module read permission, mirroring 13.1; document). The operator set (EQ, NE, GT, GTE, LT, LTE, IN, LIKE, BETWEEN, IS_NULL) and aggregation set (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX). The ROW CAP constant (10_000 per PERFORMANCE §3).
2. reporting/report_registry.py (NEW): the whitelist. A `ReportableEntity` descriptor: key (e.g. "finance.journal_lines"), the ORM model class, source_permission, and a dict of allowed columns {name: ReportColumn(label, type (str/number/date/bool), filterable, groupable, is_aggregatable)}. Register a SAFE initial set across modules — e.g. finance journal lines (account, posting_date, debit, credit, amounts — NO masked data), inventory items + stock moves, sales orders, procurement POs, an HR employee entity with ONLY non-sensitive columns (code, name, department, status — explicitly EXCLUDE base_salary/national_id/etc.). Each entity declares its tenant-scoped model so the do_orm_execute filter applies. Document the whitelist + the masked-exclusion rule.
3. reporting/report_builder.py (or service/report_builder.py): `run_report(session, tenant_id, spec)` — validate the spec against the registry (unknown entity/column/operator → 400 with a clear envelope code reporting.invalid_report; a column not marked filterable/groupable used as such → 400), build the ORM select (select the requested columns OR group-by columns + aggregations; apply filters via typed bind params — coerce the filter value to the column's python type like pagination does, NEVER string-interpolate; apply group-by; ORDER BY a stable key; CAP at 10_000 rows + 1 to detect truncation), execute over the tenant-filtered session, return rows as a list of dicts (column name → value, money/qty/date as JSON-safe). Return {columns: [...], rows: [...], row_count, truncated: bool}. PERMISSION: the caller must hold the entity's source_permission (else 403). 
4. reporting/schemas.py additions: ReportSpec {entity, columns[], filters[{column, operator, value}], group_by[], aggregations[{column, func, alias}], limit?}, ReportResult {columns[], rows[], row_count, truncated}.
5. reporting/router.py additions: POST /api/v1/reporting/reports/run (body = ReportSpec → ReportResult JSON for the grid; reporting.report.run + the entity's source perm), GET /api/v1/reporting/reports/entities (list the whitelisted entities + their columns, so a UI can build the picker; reporting.report.run), POST /api/v1/reporting/reports/export (same spec → a STREAMING CSV response per PERFORMANCE §3 — use a StreamingResponse generating CSV rows lazily, not materializing 10k rows in memory; Content-Type text/csv, Content-Disposition attachment). Permission-guard; mount (it's already mounted via the reporting router — add the routes). PERFORMANCE §6 (the report query is bounded by the 10k cap; filters/group-by on indexed columns; the CSV streams).
6. docs/modules/reporting.md: add a Report Builder section (the whitelist-registry security model, entity+columns+filters+group-by+aggregations, the typed-bind no-SQL-injection construction, tenancy auto-applied via the ORM, the masked-column exclusion, the 10k cap + streaming CSV export). DECISIONS.md D-059 (the report builder: whitelist registry of reportable entities/columns gated by source permission; ORM-only construction with typed binds (tenant auto-filtered, no injection); masked/sensitive columns excluded from the whitelist; ad-hoc-only (no persisted report defs in v1); 10k cap + streaming CSV).
7. Tests: test_report_builder.py (run a report over a whitelisted entity: select columns + filter + group-by + aggregation returns the right rows; an unknown entity/column → 400; a non-filterable column used as a filter → 400; the result is TENANT-SCOPED (tenant A's report can't see tenant B's rows — the do_orm_execute filter applies); a filter value is bound not interpolated (a malicious-looking value like \"'; DROP TABLE\" is treated as data, returns no rows, doesn't error/execute — proves no injection); the 10k cap truncates + sets truncated=true (seed >cap? expensive — instead set a small limit in the spec and assert truncation flag, OR assert the cap constant is applied; a realistic smaller test: limit=2 over 3 rows → truncated true); MASKED data is NOT exposable (the HR employee entity's whitelist has no base_salary column → requesting it → 400 unknown column)), test_report_export.py (the CSV export streams the right rows + header; content-type text/csv), test_report_api.py (the entities-list endpoint, run + export endpoints, RBAC base + source perm, tenant isolation). HEED #53.

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg — the report builder must work on BOTH engines, esp. group-by/aggregation SQL portability); delete stray atlas.db; every file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 13.2 (note Phase 13 / Reporting COMPLETE) + DECISIONS.md D-059. If NO migration needed, say so. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check (esp. §5 + the model-import exception for the registry + no cycle) and report it.

Return: files created/changed, the whitelist-registry security model + the entities registered, the ORM-typed-bind no-injection construction + tenancy auto-application, the masked-column exclusion, the 10k cap + streaming CSV, whether a migration was needed, the injection + tenant-isolation tests, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), §9 self-check, deviations.

1	"""Reporting (role-based dashboards) constants (STRUCTURE §3): the dashboard permission key + the
2	KPI catalog and its KPI→source-permission GATING MAP, registered into the core RBAC catalog at
3	import (D-009 / D-058).
4	
5	A SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line cap) — PLAN
6	13.1's read-only KPI dashboard sits well under that.
7	
8	READ-ONLY (D-058). Reporting owns NO tables, NO sequences, NO document types — it is a projection
9	aggregator over OTHER modules' ``queries`` (D-021: KPIs read existing queries, never new stored
10	totals). So the only key it DECLARES is ``reporting.dashboard.read`` (base dashboard access). Every
11	individual KPI is gated by the SOURCE module's existing read permission, so the dashboard is
12	ROLE-BASED: a finance role sees finance KPIs, a sales role sees sales KPIs, and the endpoint returns
13	ONLY the KPIs the caller is permitted to see (the ``KPI_PERMISSIONS`` map below is the contract).
14	"""
15	
16	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions
17	from app.modules.finance.constants import (
18	    FINANCE_AP_READ,
19	    FINANCE_AR_READ,
20	    FINANCE_STATEMENTS_READ,
21	)
22	from app.modules.inventory.constants import INVENTORY_VALUATION_READ
23	from app.modules.procurement.constants import PROCUREMENT_PO_READ
24	from app.modules.sales.constants import SALES_ORDER_READ
25	
26	# --- The base dashboard permission (D-009 / D-058) ----------------------------
27	# The ONLY key reporting declares: holding it is the price of admission to the dashboard endpoint.
28	# Each KPI inside is then gated by the SOURCE module's read permission (KPI_PERMISSIONS below).
29	REPORTING_DASHBOARD_READ = "reporting.dashboard.read"
30	
31	register_permissions(
32	    REPORTING_DASHBOARD_READ,
33	    descriptions={
34	        REPORTING_DASHBOARD_READ: "Access the role-based KPI dashboard",
35	    },
36	)
37	
38	
39	# --- KPI catalog (D-058) ------------------------------------------------------
40	# The stable string keys the dashboard response is keyed by. Used by the service (which computes the
41	# permitted subset) and the schema (typed sub-models per KPI). Plain constants, not an enum, so the
42	# response-dict keys and the schema field names stay in lockstep with no value translation.
43	KPI_CASH_POSITION = "cash_position"
44	KPI_AR_AGING = "ar_aging"
45	KPI_AP_AGING = "ap_aging"
46	KPI_INVENTORY_VALUE = "inventory_value"
47	KPI_OPEN_SALES_ORDERS = "open_sales_orders"
48	KPI_OPEN_PURCHASE_ORDERS = "open_purchase_orders"
49	KPI_OTD_PERCENT = "otd_percent"
50	KPI_WIP_VALUE = "wip_value"
51	
52	
53	# --- THE KPI → SOURCE-PERMISSION GATING MAP (D-058, the role-based contract) ---
54	# Each KPI is computed ONLY when the caller holds the SOURCE module's read permission, so the
55	# dashboard returns only the KPIs the role can see (a finance role gets cash/AR/AP/WIP, a sales role
56	# gets open orders + OTD, an inventory role gets inventory value, a buyer gets open POs). cash + WIP
57	# read the same finance statements/journal projection, so both gate on finance.statements.read; AR
58	# aging on finance.ar.read, AP aging on finance.ap.read (the AP/AR-specific read keys). The service
59	# iterates this map: gate passes → compute the KPI, else omit it entirely from the response.
60	KPI_PERMISSIONS: dict[str, str] = {
61	    KPI_CASH_POSITION: FINANCE_STATEMENTS_READ,
62	    KPI_AR_AGING: FINANCE_AR_READ,
63	    KPI_AP_AGING: FINANCE_AP_READ,
64	    KPI_INVENTORY_VALUE: INVENTORY_VALUATION_READ,
65	    KPI_OPEN_SALES_ORDERS: SALES_ORDER_READ,
66	    KPI_OPEN_PURCHASE_ORDERS: PROCUREMENT_PO_READ,
67	    KPI_OTD_PERCENT: SALES_ORDER_READ,
68	    # WIP is the finance WIP-clearing balance (D-048/D-058 — the authoritative open-WIP figure),
69	    # so it gates on the finance statements read, NOT a manufacturing key.
70	    KPI_WIP_VALUE: FINANCE_STATEMENTS_READ,
71	}
72

1	"""Reporting (dashboard) API schemas (PLAN 13.1, D-058): the typed KPI sub-models + the dashboard
2	envelope.
3	
4	Each KPI is its own typed sub-model (a card's worth of data): ``MoneyKpi`` (a single money figure +
5	currency), ``AgingSummary`` (the four aging buckets + total), ``CountValueKpi`` (a count + a money
6	total — open orders), ``OtdKpi`` (an on-time-delivery percentage + its numerator/denominator). The
7	``DashboardResponse`` holds every KPI as an OPTIONAL field: the role-based endpoint returns ONLY the
8	KPIs the caller is permitted to see (a missing permission ⇒ that field is ``None`` and is omitted
9	from the JSON), so the response shape IS the role (D-058).
10	
11	MONEY AS STRINGS (build-spec §13.1). Dashboard money fields serialize as STRINGS, not JSON numbers —
12	a KPI card is a display surface read by JS clients where a float round-trip would corrupt the exact
13	decimal. ``MoneyStr`` is a ``Decimal`` annotated with a ``PlainSerializer`` that renders the exact
14	decimal string (the value stays a ``Decimal`` in Python for arithmetic; only the wire form is a
15	string). ``percent`` is a plain number (it is a ratio, not money).
16	"""
17	
18	from decimal import Decimal
19	from typing import Annotated
20	
21	from pydantic import PlainSerializer
22	
23	from app.core.schemas import ApiModel
24	
25	# A money Decimal that serializes to its exact decimal STRING on the wire (build-spec §13.1). The
26	# value remains a Decimal in Python; only JSON rendering differs from the number-valued money in the
27	# transactional Read schemas.
28	MoneyStr = Annotated[Decimal, PlainSerializer(lambda v: str(v), return_type=str)]
29	
30	
31	class MoneyKpi(ApiModel):
32	    """A single-figure money KPI card (D-058): cash position, inventory value, WIP value. ``value``
33	    is the exact decimal as a string; ``currency`` is the tenant's functional currency code."""
34	
35	    value: MoneyStr
36	    currency: str
37	
38	
39	class AgingSummary(ApiModel):
40	    """An AR/AP aging KPI card (D-058): the rolled-up bucket totals (current / 1-30 / 31-60 / 90+) +
41	    grand total — the dashboard collapses the aging report's 61-90 + over-90 tail into one 90+
42	    bucket. Money fields are exact-decimal strings. ``currency`` names the figures' currency."""
43	
44	    current: MoneyStr
45	    d30: MoneyStr
46	    d60: MoneyStr
47	    d90plus: MoneyStr
48	    total: MoneyStr
49	    currency: str
50	
51	
52	class CountValueKpi(ApiModel):
53	    """An open-orders KPI card (D-058): a count of documents + their summed money value (open sales
54	    orders, open purchase orders). ``total`` is the exact-decimal string."""
55	
56	    count: int
57	    total: MoneyStr
58	    currency: str
59	
60	
61	class OtdKpi(ApiModel):
62	    """The on-time-delivery KPI card (D-058): the percentage of measured deliveries that shipped on
63	    or before the order's requested date, plus its numerator/denominator. ``percent`` is a ratio (0-
64	    100), rounded to one decimal; ``total`` 0 ⇒ no measurable deliveries (percent presents as 0)."""
65	
66	    percent: float
67	    on_time: int
68	    total: int
69

1	"""D-014 keyset (seek) pagination — never OFFSET.
2	
3	Cursor browsing is O(page) at any depth and stable under concurrent inserts (the ERP norm for
4	ledger/list browsing). Every list orders by a whitelisted sort column plus the PK ``id`` as a
5	mandatory unique tiebreaker (``ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC``), fetches ``limit + 1`` rows,
6	and emits ``next_cursor`` from the last RETURNED row only when the extra row arrived.
7	
8	**Cursor.** ``base64url(JSON)`` of ``{"v":1, "k":[last sort values..., last id], "s": sort-spec,
9	"q": filter fingerprint}`` — opaque to clients, validated server-side. ``v``, ``s`` and ``q`` must
10	match the current request (a cursor minted for one query/sort/filter can't be replayed on
11	another) → 400 ``pagination.invalid_cursor`` on any mismatch or tamper.
12	
13	**Seek predicate.** Written in the EXPANDED portable OR-form
14	``col0 < k0 OR (col0 = k0 AND col1 < k1) OR (... AND id < kN)`` (directions flipped per column for
15	ASC). D-014 mandates this expansion because SQLite lacks MIXED-direction row-value comparison —
16	``(a, b) > (x, y)`` only works when every column sorts the same way, and our lists mix ASC/DESC
17	freely — so the expansion is the only form correct on BOTH engines (verified: this project's
18	aiosqlite, 3.53, DOES support uniform-direction row-values, but the expanded form is used
19	unconditionally so a mixed-direction sort is never silently wrong).
20	
21	**Placement deviation.** D-014's letter puts ``paginate`` in ``core/db.py`` and the cursor codec
22	in ``core/schemas.py``. The keyset machinery (codec + fingerprint + expanded predicate +
23	CursorParams) is substantial and cross-cutting, so it gets its own flat core file per STRUCTURE
24	§8.5 ("one concept per file") — a justified core addition recorded in DECISIONS.md, the same way
25	core/money.py and core/custom_fields.py were. The ``Page`` envelope stays in core/schemas.py.
26	"""
27	
28	import base64
29	import binascii
30	import hashlib
31	import json
32	import uuid
33	from dataclasses import dataclass
34	from datetime import date, datetime
35	from decimal import Decimal
36	from enum import StrEnum
37	from typing import Any
38	
39	import sqlalchemy as sa
40	from pydantic import BaseModel
41	from sqlalchemy import Select
42	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
43	from sqlalchemy.orm import InstrumentedAttribute
44	
45	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
46	from app.core.schemas import Page
47	
48	DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50
49	MAX_LIMIT = 200
50	_CURSOR_VERSION = 1
51	
52	
53	class SortDirection(StrEnum):
54	    ASC = "asc"
55	    DESC = "desc"
56	
57	
58	@dataclass(frozen=True)
59	class OrderKey:
60	    """One whitelisted sort column + direction. ``paginate`` always appends the PK as the final
61	    tiebreaker, so a list declares only its business sort columns (e.g. created_at DESC)."""
62	
63	    column: InstrumentedAttribute[Any]
64	    direction: SortDirection = SortDirection.ASC
65	
66	    @property
67	    def name(self) -> str:
68	        return self.column.key
69	
70	
71	def _sort_spec(order_keys: list[OrderKey]) -> str:
72	    """Stable string identity of the sort (``'created_at:desc,id:asc'``), embedded in the cursor
73	    so a cursor minted under one ordering is rejected if the request's ordering changed."""
74	    return ",".join(f"{key.name}:{key.direction.value}" for key in order_keys)
75	
76	
77	def _encode_value(value: Any) -> Any:
78	    """Serialize a sort-key value to a JSON-safe, round-trippable form. datetimes/dates go to ISO
79	    strings, Decimals to strings (exact, consistent with D-015), UUIDs to str; primitives pass."""
80	    if isinstance(value, datetime | date):
81	        return value.isoformat()
82	    if isinstance(value, Decimal):
83	        return str(value)
84	    if isinstance(value, bool | int | float | str) or value is None:
85	        return value
86	    return str(value)
87	
88	
89	def encode_cursor(key_values: list[Any], sort_spec: str, filter_fingerprint: str) -> str:
90	    """base64url(JSON) of the last row's key tuple + the sort/filter fingerprints (D-014)."""
91	    payload = {
92	        "v": _CURSOR_VERSION,
93	        "k": [_encode_value(value) for value in key_values],
94	        "s": sort_spec,
95	        "q": filter_fingerprint,
96	    }
97	    raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
98	    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).decode("ascii")
99	
100	
101	def decode_cursor(cursor: str, sort_spec: str, filter_fingerprint: str) -> list[Any]:
102	    """Decode and validate a cursor, returning its key tuple. Any tamper, malformed payload, wrong
103	    version, or a sort/filter fingerprint that does not match the CURRENT request raises 400
104	    ``pagination.invalid_cursor`` — a cursor cannot be replayed on a different query (D-014)."""
105	    try:
106	        raw = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(cursor.encode("ascii"))
107	        payload = json.loads(raw)
108	    except (binascii.Error, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
109	        raise _invalid_cursor() from exc
110	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
111	        raise _invalid_cursor()
112	    if (
113	        payload.get("v") != _CURSOR_VERSION
114	        or payload.get("s") != sort_spec
115	        or payload.get("q") != filter_fingerprint
116	        or not isinstance(payload.get("k"), list)
117	    ):
118	        raise _invalid_cursor()
119	    return payload["k"]

121	
122	def _invalid_cursor() -> ValidationFailedError:
123	    return ValidationFailedError(
124	        message="The pagination cursor is invalid for this query",
125	        code="pagination.invalid_cursor",
126	    )

128	
129	def filter_fingerprint(*parts: Any) -> str:
130	    """sha256-prefix of normalized filter parts (D-014). Routers pass whatever WHERE inputs scope
131	    the list (status, date range, search term…); a different filter set yields a different
132	    fingerprint, so a cursor from one filtered view can't bleed into another. Empty parts → the
133	    fingerprint of an empty filter set, still stable."""
134	    canonical = json.dumps([_encode_value(part) for part in parts], separators=(",", ":"))
135	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
136	
137	
138	def _coerce_key_value(column: InstrumentedAttribute[Any], value: Any) -> Any:
139	    """Coerce a decoded cursor value back to the column's Python type so the seek comparison binds
140	    correctly on both engines. datetimes/dates and Decimals were ISO/str-encoded; the rest are
141	    JSON primitives that bind as-is (SQLAlchemy adapts UUID/str columns from the str form)."""
142	    python_type = getattr(column.type, "python_type", None)
143	    if value is None or python_type is None or not isinstance(value, str):
144	        return value
145	    if python_type is datetime:
146	        return datetime.fromisoformat(value)
147	    if python_type is date:
148	        return date.fromisoformat(value)
149	    if python_type is Decimal:
150	        return Decimal(value)
151	    if python_type is uuid.UUID:
152	        # The PK tiebreaker is a UUID column; SQLAlchemy's Uuid type binds a uuid.UUID, not the
153	        # str it was cursor-encoded as, so re-parse it here (else the bind processor blows up).
154	        return uuid.UUID(value)
155	    return value
156	
157	
158	def _seek_predicate(order_keys: list[OrderKey], key_values: list[Any]) -> sa.ColumnElement[bool]:
159	    """Build the expanded OR-form seek predicate (D-014). For sort columns c0..cN with the values
160	    from the previous page's last row, the predicate selecting STRICTLY-AFTER rows is::
161	
162	        cmp(c0)
163	        OR (c0 == v0 AND cmp(c1))
164	        OR (c0 == v0 AND c1 == v1 AND cmp(c2))
165	        ...
166	
167	    where ``cmp`` is ``<`` for a DESC column and ``>`` for ASC. The PK tiebreaker is already the
168	    last OrderKey, so every distinct row is on exactly one side of the boundary — no skips, no
169	    duplicates, even when earlier sort columns tie. Expanded (not row-value) so mixed ASC/DESC is
170	    correct on SQLite too."""
171	    coerced = [
172	        _coerce_key_value(key.column, value)
173	        for key, value in zip(order_keys, key_values, strict=True)
174	    ]
175	    clauses: list[sa.ColumnElement[bool]] = []
176	    for i, key in enumerate(order_keys):
177	        equals = [order_keys[j].column == coerced[j] for j in range(i)]
178	        strict = (
179	            key.column > coerced[i]
180	            if key.direction is SortDirection.ASC
181	            else key.column < coerced[i]
182	        )
183	        clauses.append(sa.and_(*equals, strict))
184	    return sa.or_(*clauses)
185	
186	
187	def _apply_order(stmt: Select[Any], order_keys: list[OrderKey]) -> Select[Any]:
188	    return stmt.order_by(
189	        *(
190	            key.column.asc() if key.direction is SortDirection.ASC else key.column.desc()
191	            for key in order_keys
192	        )
193	    )

195	
196	async def paginate[T](
197	    session: AsyncSession,
198	    stmt: Select[tuple[T]],
199	    *,
200	    order_by: list[OrderKey],
201	    pk: InstrumentedAttribute[Any],
202	    cursor: str | None = None,
203	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
204	    filters: str = "",
205	) -> Page[T]:
206	    """Keyset-paginate ``stmt`` and return a ``Page[T]`` (D-014). ``order_by`` is the whitelisted
207	    business sort; ``pk`` (the model's id) is appended as the mandatory unique tiebreaker so the
208	    cursor is stable. ``filters`` is the router's filter fingerprint (see
209	    :func:`filter_fingerprint`) baked into the cursor. The single generic helper module routers
210	    use — they never hand-roll keyset SQL.
211	
212	    Fetches ``limit + 1`` rows; if the extra row arrives, the page is full and ``next_cursor`` is
213	    minted from the LAST returned row's sort-key tuple. The cursor (when present) is decoded and
214	    validated against this request's sort + filter fingerprint, then turned into the expanded-OR
215	    seek predicate that selects strictly-after rows."""
216	    if limit < 1:
217	        limit = 1
218	    keys = [*order_by, OrderKey(pk, SortDirection.ASC)]
219	    sort_spec = _sort_spec(keys)
220	
221	    seek_stmt = stmt
222	    if cursor is not None:
223	        key_values = decode_cursor(cursor, sort_spec, filters)
224	        if len(key_values) != len(keys):
225	            raise _invalid_cursor()
226	        seek_stmt = seek_stmt.where(_seek_predicate(keys, key_values))
227	
228	    seek_stmt = _apply_order(seek_stmt, keys).limit(limit + 1)
229	    rows = list((await session.execute(seek_stmt)).scalars().all())
230	
231	    has_more = len(rows) > limit
232	    items = rows[:limit]
233	    next_cursor: str | None = None
234	    if has_more and items:
235	        last = items[-1]
236	        next_cursor = encode_cursor(
237	            [getattr(last, key.name) for key in keys], sort_spec, filters
238	        )
239	    return Page(items=items, next_cursor=next_cursor, limit=limit)
240	
241	
242	def map_page[S: BaseModel](page: Page[Any], schema: type[S]) -> Page[S]:
243	    """Validate a service-layer ``Page`` of ORM rows into its wire schema — the one-line router
244	    epilogue for every paginated list endpoint, so the items/next_cursor/limit plumbing is never
245	    hand-rolled (and the envelope can't drift between endpoints)."""
246	    return Page(
247	        items=[schema.model_validate(item) for item in page.items],
248	        next_cursor=page.next_cursor,
249	        limit=page.limit,
250	    )
251	
252	
253	@dataclass(frozen=True)
254	class CursorParams:
255	    """Parsed ``?cursor=&limit=`` query params (D-014). ``limit`` is clamped to ``[1, MAX_LIMIT]``
256	    and defaults to ``DEFAULT_LIMIT``, so a client can never request an unbounded page. A router
257	    declares ``params: CursorParamsDep`` and forwards ``params.cursor`` / ``params.limit`` to
258	    :func:`paginate`."""
259	
260	    cursor: str | None
261	    limit: int
262	
263	
264	def cursor_params(cursor: str | None = None, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT) -> CursorParams:
265	    """FastAPI dependency parsing the cursor/limit query params with the max-limit cap (D-014)."""
266	    clamped = max(1, min(limit, MAX_LIMIT))
267	    return CursorParams(cursor=cursor, limit=clamped)
268	
269	
270	__all__ = [
271	    "DEFAULT_LIMIT",
272	    "MAX_LIMIT",
273	    "CursorParams",

275	    "SortDirection",
276	    "cursor_params",
277	    "decode_cursor",
278	    "encode_cursor",
279	    "filter_fingerprint",

1	"""D-007 tenancy enforcement: context, non-bypassable session filter, write stamping.
2	
3	Three of the four cooperating D-007 layers live here:
4	1. Context — the `current_tenant_id` ContextVar (set by core/deps.py after JWT
5	   validation from PLAN 3.3 on; by `tenant_context()` in tests and seed).
6	2. Read/write filtering — the `do_orm_execute` listener.
7	3. Write stamping — the `before_flush` listener.
8	The fourth layer (composite FKs + the SQLite FK pragma) lives in core/models.py
9	and core/db.py.
10	"""
11	
12	import uuid
13	from collections.abc import Iterator
14	from contextlib import contextmanager
15	from contextvars import ContextVar
16	from itertools import chain
17	
18	from sqlalchemy import event
19	from sqlalchemy.orm import ORMExecuteState, Session, with_loader_criteria
20	
21	from app.core.exceptions import TenancyError
22	from app.core.models import TenantMixin
23	
24	current_tenant_id: ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None] = ContextVar("current_tenant_id", default=None)
25	_system_context: ContextVar[bool] = ContextVar("system_context", default=False)
26	
27	
28	def get_current_tenant_id() -> uuid.UUID | None:
29	    """Active tenant id, fail-closed: raises unless a tenant context is set.
30	    Returns None only while system_context() is active."""
31	    tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
32	    if tenant_id is None and not _system_context.get():
33	        raise TenancyError("No tenant context is active")
34	    return tenant_id
35	
36	
37	@contextmanager
38	def tenant_context(tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> Iterator[None]:
39	    """Run the block as one tenant (tests, seed transaction phase; request handling
40	    sets the ContextVar directly in core/deps.py with middleware reset, per D-007)."""
41	    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
42	    try:
43	        yield
44	    finally:
45	        current_tenant_id.reset(token)
46	
47	
48	@contextmanager
49	def system_context() -> Iterator[None]:
50	    """Suspend tenant filtering and write stamping for the block.
51	
52	    Sanctioned in exactly four greppable app call sites (D-007):
53	    1. login user-lookup (core/auth, PLAN 3.3);
54	    2. tenant provisioning in modules/admin (PLAN 14.2);
55	    3. Alembic/seed provisioning phase (seed.py, PLAN 16);
56	    4. event-bus system-event replay (core/events, PLAN 3.6).
57	    Test fixtures may also use it (D-025 tenant_factory). Writers under system
58	    context must set tenant_id explicitly; the composite-FK backstop still applies.
59	    """
60	    token = _system_context.set(True)
61	    try:
62	        yield
63	    finally:
64	        _system_context.reset(token)
65	
66	
67	def _involves_tenant_scoped_entities(execute_state: ORMExecuteState) -> bool:
68	    # all_mappers inspects select() column descriptions / mapper entities AND the
69	    # bind mapper of ORM-enabled update()/delete() — the D-007 involvement rule.
70	    return any(issubclass(m.class_, TenantMixin) for m in execute_state.all_mappers)
71	
72	
73	def _filter_tenant_statements(execute_state: ORMExecuteState) -> None:
74	    """do_orm_execute listener: inject the tenant predicate into every ORM
75	    select/update/delete; fail-closed when tenant-scoped entities are touched
76	    without a tenant context."""
77	    if not execute_state.is_orm_statement:
78	        # Core statements bypass by design: sanctioned only inside core/ with
79	        # explicit tenant_id, bounded by the D-007 grep gate.
80	        return
81	    if execute_state.is_column_load or execute_state.is_relationship_load:
82	        # Refresh and lazy loads inherit the criteria propagated from their
83	        # originating statement; re-injecting here would break attribute refresh.
84	        return
85	    if not (execute_state.is_select or execute_state.is_update or execute_state.is_delete):
86	        return
87	    if _system_context.get():
88	        return
89	    tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
90	    if tenant_id is None:
91	        if _involves_tenant_scoped_entities(execute_state):
92	            raise TenancyError("Tenant-scoped statement executed without a tenant context")
93	        # Statements touching only non-tenant tables (Alembic bookkeeping, the
94	        # tenants root) legitimately run with no tenant context.
95	        return
96	    execute_state.statement = execute_state.statement.options(
97	        with_loader_criteria(
98	            TenantMixin,
99	            # The ContextVar is read above, in this per-execution listener — the
100	            # lambda-SQL system forbids invoking .get() inside the lambda itself.
101	            # track_closure_variables=False keeps the closure value out of the
102	            # statement cache key, so each execution binds the fresh tenant id
103	            # instead of baking in the first value seen (pinned by a test).
104	            lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == tenant_id,
105	            include_aliases=True,
106	            track_closure_variables=False,
107	        )
108	    )
109	
110	
111	def _stamp_tenant_on_flush(session: Session, flush_context: object, instances: object) -> None:
112	    """before_flush listener: stamp tenant_id on new tenant-scoped instances and
113	    reject any new/dirty instance whose tenant_id differs from the context."""
114	    if _system_context.get():
115	        # Provisioning/seed/system writes set tenant_id explicitly; the composite
116	        # FK backstop still rejects ids that do not exist in adm_tenants.
117	        return
118	    active = current_tenant_id.get()
119	    for obj in chain(session.new, session.dirty):
120	        if not isinstance(obj, TenantMixin):
121	            continue
122	        if active is None:
123	            raise TenancyError("Tenant-scoped instance flushed without a tenant context")
124	        if obj.tenant_id is None:
125	            obj.tenant_id = active
126	        elif obj.tenant_id != active:
127	            raise TenancyError(
128	                "Instance tenant_id differs from the active tenant context",
129	                code="tenancy.tenant_mismatch",
130	            )
131	
132	
133	def install_tenancy_guards() -> None:
134	    """Attach both listeners to the sync Session class — AsyncSession proxies it,
135	    so every execute call and relationship load is covered. Idempotent so repeated
136	    calls cannot double-register. Invoked at import time of app.core.db: every
137	    engine/session factory in app, tests and seed is built from that module, so no
138	    session can exist unguarded (models.py cannot host the call — this module
139	    imports TenantMixin from it, which would be an import cycle)."""
140	    if not event.contains(Session, "do_orm_execute", _filter_tenant_statements):
141	        event.listen(Session, "do_orm_execute", _filter_tenant_statements)
142	    if not event.contains(Session, "before_flush", _stamp_tenant_on_flush):
143	        event.listen(Session, "before_flush", _stamp_tenant_on_flush)
144

2	
3	This is the ONE place that sets `current_tenant_id` for the request lifecycle from a
4	validated access token; the pure-ASGI middleware in app.main resets it in a finally
5	block so request A's tenant never leaks to request B on the same worker.
6	"""
7	
8	import uuid
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	from typing import Annotated
11	
12	from fastapi import Depends
13	from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker
16	
17	from app.core.audit import actor_user_id_ctx
18	from app.core.auth import decode_token
19	from app.core.config import get_settings
20	from app.core.db import get_session, get_session_factory
21	from app.core.exceptions import AuthError
22	from app.core.models import User
23	from app.core.rbac import current_permissions, resolve_permissions
24	from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
25	
26	# get_session / get_settings are re-exported so routers depend on a single core.deps
27	# surface rather than reaching into core.db / core.config directly.
28	__all__ = [
29	    "CurrentUser",
30	    "CurrentUserDep",
31	    "SessionDep",
32	    "SessionFactoryDep",
33	    "get_current_user",
34	    "get_session",
35	    "get_session_factory",
36	    "get_settings",
37	]
38	
39	# auto_error=False: a missing/blank header must surface as the D-014 auth envelope
40	# (AuthError -> 401), not Starlette's bare 403 HTTPException.
41	_bearer_scheme = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)
42	
43	# Annotated dependency aliases: the modern FastAPI idiom that keeps Depends() out of
44	# parameter defaults (ruff B008) and lets routers share one typed handle.
45	SessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)]
46	# The sessionmaker dependency (test-overridable like get_session). Job-submitting routers pass
47	# it to schedule_job post-commit so the runner opens its sessions against the SAME database —
48	# the app factory in production, the per-test engine's factory under the conftest override.
49	SessionFactoryDep = Annotated[async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], Depends(get_session_factory)]
50	_CredentialsDep = Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(_bearer_scheme)]
51	
52	
53	@dataclass(frozen=True)
54	class CurrentUser:
55	    """Resolved request principal (D-008/D-009). `permissions` is the effective key set
56	    resolved by RBAC (one join query, cached 60s)."""
57	
58	    user_id: uuid.UUID
59	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
60	    permissions: frozenset[str]
61	    token_version: int
62	
63	
64	async def get_current_user(
65	    credentials: _CredentialsDep,
66	    session: SessionDep,
67	) -> CurrentUser:
68	    if credentials is None:
69	        raise AuthError(message="Missing bearer token", code="auth.invalid_token")
70	
71	    claims = decode_token(credentials.credentials, expected_typ="access")
72	    try:
73	        user_id = uuid.UUID(claims["sub"])
74	        tenant_id = uuid.UUID(claims["tenant_id"])
75	        claim_version = int(claims["ver"])
76	    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
77	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token") from exc
78	
79	    # Set the tenancy ContextVar FROM the validated token (D-007 production setter):
80	    # the user lookup below then runs under the token's tenant, so a tampered
81	    # tenant_id can only ever resolve a user that actually belongs to that tenant —
82	    # cross-tenant access is impossible. The middleware resets this in a finally block.
83	    current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
84	
85	    user = (
86	        await session.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
87	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
88	    if user is None or not user.is_active:
89	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
90	    if user.token_version != claim_version:
91	        # Stale token after a "revoke everything" bump (D-008).
92	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
93	
94	    # RBAC resolution (D-009): one join query, memoized 60s on
95	    # (tenant_id, user_id, token_version). Runs under the tenant context set above, so
96	    # the user_roles/role_permissions rows are already tenant-filtered.
97	    permissions = await resolve_permissions(
98	        session, user.id, user.tenant_id, user.token_version
99	    )
100	    # Serialization-time masking (D-009) reads this ContextVar; the middleware resets it
101	    # in a finally block alongside current_tenant_id so it never leaks across requests.
102	    current_permissions.set(permissions)
103	    # D-010 audit context: now that the principal is known, stamp the actor onto every
104	    # audit row this request writes. The middleware seeded it None (system) and resets it.
105	    actor_user_id_ctx.set(user.id)
106	
107	    return CurrentUser(
108	        user_id=user.id,
109	        tenant_id=user.tenant_id,
110	        permissions=permissions,
111	        token_version=user.token_version,
112	    )
113	
114	
115	CurrentUserDep = Annotated[CurrentUser, Depends(get_current_user)]

content.content:
## D-014 — API envelope (keyset pagination + error shape + DB-guard error translation)

**Decision.**
**List envelope** in `core/schemas.py`: `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": str|null, "limit": int}` — no total counts (a separate aggregate endpoint serves dashboards).

**Keyset (seek) pagination only, never OFFSET:** every list orders by a whitelisted sort column plus `id` as mandatory unique tiebreaker (e.g. `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC`); fetch limit+1 rows (default 50, max 200); emit next_cursor from the last returned row when limit+1 arrived. **Cursor:** `base64url(JSON)` of `{"v":1, "k":[last sort value ISO-serialized, last id], "s":"created_at:desc", "q": sha256-prefix of normalized filters}`; opaque to clients, validated server-side — v, s, q must match the current request (mismatch → 400 `'cursor_invalid'`); seek predicate written in the expanded portable form `sort_col < :k0 OR (sort_col = :k0 AND id < :k1)` because SQLite lacks mixed-direction row-value comparison. One generic helper `paginate(session, stmt, sort, cursor, limit)` lives in `core/db.py` (cursor codec + envelope models in `core/schemas.py`); module routers never hand-roll pagination.

**Error envelope** on every non-2xx: `{"error": {"code", "message", "details": list|null, "request_id"}}`; codes are machine-readable, dot-namespaced for domain rules (`'finance.period_closed'`, `'finance.journal_unbalanced'`, `'idempotency_key_reuse'`) and generic for transport (`'validation_error'`, `'not_found'`, `'permission_denied'`, `'unauthorized'`, `'conflict'`, `'internal_error'`). `core/exceptions.py`: `AtlasError` hierarchy (NotFoundError→404, PermissionDeniedError→403, ConflictError→409, DomainRuleError(code, message)→422, TenancyError→403), handlers for AtlasError, RequestValidationError (code `'validation_error'`, details flattened to `[{field, message, type}]`), and a catch-all 500 logging request_id.

**Cross-decision glue (added):** a `DBAPIError` translator in the same file maps trigger-raised tokens to envelope codes — it matches the `'ATLAS_'` substring across IntegrityError, OperationalError, and generic DBAPIError because SQLite `RAISE(ABORT)` surfaces as IntegrityError while asyncpg plpgsql RAISE surfaces differently: `ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED`→`'finance.period_closed'` 422, `ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY`→`'finance.journal_unbalanced'` 422, `ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE`→`'finance.entry_immutable'` 422, `ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY`→`'internal_error'` 500 — so the DB backstops surface through the same envelope as service checks, pinned by tests on both engines. `request_id` comes from the audit middleware's `RequestContext` and is echoed as `X-Request-Id` on every response.

**Rationale.**
Keyset pagination is O(page) at any depth and stable under concurrent inserts — the ERP norm for ledger browsing — and works identically on both engines with the expanded predicate. Fingerprinting sort+filters into the cursor catches the classic changed-filters-mid-pagination bug. One error shape with machine codes gives `apiClient.ts` a single error path and lets tests assert codes; the trigger-token translator is what makes "enforced at service AND DB level" present a uniform API face instead of leaking raw 500s when a backstop fires.

**Rejected alternatives.**
- OFFSET/LIMIT: linear degradation and phantom/duplicate rows under concurrent posting.
- HMAC-signed cursors: the seek values are data the client already saw; fingerprint validation already rejects malformed use.
- RFC 7807 problem+json: fine standard, but the single prescribed envelope is simpler and the constraint says "consistent error envelope".
- Total counts per page: `COUNT(*)` over million-row journals per request.

**Risks & mitigations.**
- No jump-to-page-N — accepted; the DataGrid uses infinite scroll/next-page semantics.
- Sorting by mutable columns can re-show moved rows — default sorts use immutable created_at/doc_no.
- Each whitelisted sort column needs a composite index — the per-endpoint whitelist is small and indexes are declared beside it.

---

## D-015 — Money and quantity representation (exact on both engines)

This document is the implementation contract derived from the Phase-2 architecture review. Each section below is a numbered decision (D-007 … D-026), also indexed in [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md). Implementers must follow these mechanisms exactly — table names, API names, constraint semantics, trigger behavior, and parameter values are normative, not illustrative. Any change requires a superseding DECISIONS.md entry referencing the decision it replaces.

---

## D-007 — Tenancy enforcement (non-bypassable session filter)

**Decision.**
Three cooperating layers live in `core/tenancy.py` + `core/db.py`:

1. **Context.** A `ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None]` named `current_tenant_id`, set only by `get_current_user` in `core/deps.py` after JWT validation (and by the refresh endpoint directly from the validated refresh-token `tenant_id` claim — refresh does NOT use `system_context`), reset via token in a `finally` block by a pure-ASGI middleware.
2. **Read/write filtering.** A global `@event.listens_for(Session, "do_orm_execute")` hook on the sync `Session` class (`AsyncSession` proxies it, so it covers all execute calls and relationship/lazy loads) adds `with_loader_criteria(TenantMixin, lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == current_tenant_id.get(), include_aliases=True, track_closure_variables=False)` to every ORM statement, including ORM-enabled `update()`/`delete()`. **Fail-closed:** if the statement touches any `TenantMixin` mapper and `current_tenant_id` is unset, raise `TenancyError` — unless the `system_context()` ContextVar (also in `core/tenancy.py`) is active. `system_context` is invoked in exactly four greppable places: login user-lookup, tenant provisioning in admin, Alembic/seed provisioning phase, and bus system-event replay.
3. **Write stamping.** A `before_flush` listener stamps `tenant_id` on new `TenantMixin` objects when unset and raises `TenancyError` when a new/dirty object's `tenant_id` differs from the context.
4. **DB backstop.** Every FK between tenant-scoped tables is composite `(tenant_id, <entity>_id)` referencing `UNIQUE (tenant_id, id)` on the parent, declared via a `tenant_fk()` helper in `core/models.py`. **Critical SQLite fix:** SQLite only enforces FKs with `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, so `core/db.py` registers an engine `connect` event that emits the pragma on every SQLite connection (runtime, tests, seed) — without this the backstop silently does nothing on the test engine.

Core-level statements (Core `Table` inserts, `text()`) bypass the ORM hook; they are sanctioned only inside `core/` (audit writer, numbering, idempotency) where `tenant_id` is always explicit, enforced by a CI grep gate banning `text(` and Core `.insert(` under `app/modules/` (`tests/` is exempt — DB-guard tests need raw SQL).

Non-bypassability tests in `tests/core/test_tenancy.py` iterate `Base.registry.mappers` so new models are auto-covered. For every `TenantMixin` mapper assert: (a) bare `select()` under tenant A returns zero tenant-B rows; (b) relationship loads never leak; (c) ORM `update()` with no WHERE touches only tenant-A rows; (d) execution with unset ContextVar raises; (e) inserting a foreign `tenant_id` raises; (f) `session.get(cls, b_id)` under tenant A returns `None`.

**Rationale.**
`do_orm_execute` + `with_loader_criteria` is the only SQLAlchemy 2.0 mechanism that injects criteria into every ORM statement — including lazy loads and bulk ORM writes — with zero cooperation from query authors, which is the literal "cannot bypass" requirement. ContextVar is async-task-safe under FastAPI. Fail-closed converts "forgot to set tenant" from a leak into a hard error. Composite FKs give a schema-level invariant on both engines, but only if the SQLite FK pragma is actually on — the original draft omitted that, which would have made the backstop a no-op exactly where CI runs. Mapper-enumerating tests make the guarantee self-extending.

**Rejected alternatives.**
- PostgreSQL RLS with `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id`: unprovable in the SQLite CI/demo run, so it cannot be the primary mechanism; noted in DECISIONS.md as Postgres-only hardening post-v1.
- Per-query `.where()` helpers or custom Query base: bypassable by anyone writing `select()` directly.
- Schema- or database-per-tenant: contradicts the mandated row-level design and makes provisioning/Alembic disproportionately heavy.
- Mapper write-events only: guards writes, not reads.

**Risks & mitigations.**
- Raw SQL and Core statements bypass the hook — bounded by the grep gate, the composite-FK backstop, and review; residual gap recorded in DECISIONS.md.
- Identity-map hits (`session.get`) skip SQL — benign because the request-scoped session only ever holds same-tenant rows; sessions are never shared across requests.
- `track_closure_variables=False` is mandatory so the lambda re-reads the ContextVar per execution instead of baking in the first value seen; a dedicated test executes the same statement under two tenants in one process to pin this.

---

## D-008 — Auth token flow (JWT access+refresh, rotation with grace window, argon2)

**Decision.**
PyJWT, HS256, single `ATLAS_JWT_SECRET` (env, >=64 random bytes).

- **Access token:** 15-min TTL (`ATLAS_JWT_ACCESS_TTL_SECONDS`), claims `{sub: user_id, tenant_id, sid: refresh-session id, ver: user.token_version, typ: 'access', jti, iat, exp}`. Stateless, but `ver` is compared against `core_users.token_version` (the user row is loaded anyway for RBAC), so "revoke everything" = increment `token_version`. No permissions in the token.
=====D-009=====
## D-009 — RBAC data model, permission dependency, field masking

**Decision.**
Four tables:

- `core_permissions` (id, key UNIQUE like `'finance.journal.post'`, description) — a global code-defined catalog: each module declares keys as constants in its `constants.py`, a registry in `core/rbac.py` collects them, and startup sync + `seed.py` upsert the catalog; permissions are not tenant-editable.
- `core_roles` (id, tenant_id, name, description, is_system; UNIQUE(tenant_id, name)) — tenant-scoped, system roles seeded from industry templates at provisioning.
- `core_role_permissions` (role_id, permission_id, composite PK).
- `core_user_roles` (tenant_id, user_id, role_id, composite PK).

**Check path:** `require_permission(key)` factory in `core/rbac.py` returns an async dependency depending on `get_current_user`; effective permissions resolved once per request by one join query (user_roles ⋈ role_permissions ⋈ permissions), memoized in an in-process TTL cache (60 s) keyed `(tenant_id, user_id, token_version)`; missing key → 403 with envelope code `'permission_denied'` naming the key. Routers attach per route: `dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(FIN_JOURNAL_POST))]`. The resolved frozenset lands on `CurrentUser` and in a `current_permissions` ContextVar set by `get_current_user`.

**Field-level read masking** (HR compensation/IDs): a `Masked(tp, permission)` factory in `core/schemas.py` returning `Annotated[tp | None, WrapSerializer(functools.partial(_mask_serializer, permission))]` — the permission is bound via `functools.partial` closure (NOT loose Annotated metadata, which a WrapSerializer cannot read); the serializer reads `current_permissions` at serialization time and returns the real value only if the key (e.g. `'hr.employee.read_compensation'`) is present, else `None`. Works under `response_model` serialization without plumbing `SerializationInfo.context`.

**Write side:** masked fields are excluded from the entity's Update schema and live behind a separate endpoint+schema guarded by the corresponding update permission, so a partial update can never silently null compensation.

**Rationale.**
Tenant-scoped roles over a code-owned catalog satisfies "RBAC as data" while preventing tenants from inventing keys no code checks. One resolution query + short TTL cache makes per-route checks O(1) without baking stale permissions into JWTs (revocation lands within 60 s, or instantly via `token_version` bump which changes the cache key). The partial-bound WrapSerializer is idiomatic Pydantic v2, declares the guarding permission on the field itself, and centralizes masking in one core construct. Masking to `None` keeps response types honest for the TypeScript mirror (`field: string | null`).

**Rejected alternatives.**
- Permissions embedded in JWT: stale for 15 min and bloats the token; the user row is loaded anyway.
- Per-tenant permission catalogs: orphan keys nothing enforces.
- Casbin/oso engines: external DSLs fight "RBAC as data + service layer owns logic" and complicate the dual-engine story.
- Per-schema `computed_field` masking: scatters security logic across modules.
- `response_model_exclude` per route: route-level, not principal-level, and drifts silently.

**Risks & mitigations.**
- ContextVar-dependent serialization masks everything outside a request (tests, jobs) — fail-closed and correct; the test harness provides a `permissions_context` fixture that sets the ContextVar explicitly.
- TTL cache lags grants up to 60 s per process (multi-worker deploys lag per worker) — documented; admin "revoke now" bumps `token_version`.
- Masked-`None` is ambiguous with genuinely-null values for authorized readers — accepted for v1; add a sibling `is_masked` boolean in the same serializer if it bites.

---

## D-010 — Audit capture (split-phase session-event diffs + middleware context)

**Decision.**
Two layers with disjoint responsibilities in `core/audit.py`.

**Data layer**, split across three Session events to be correct about both attribute history and generated PKs:

1. `before_flush` walks `session.dirty` and `session.deleted` for `AuditMixin` models and computes per-column diffs from `inspect(obj).attrs[col].history` (`{field: {old, new}}` for changed columns; old values for deletes) — history is only guaranteed pre-flush, so updates/deletes are captured here, not in `after_flush` as the original draft had it.
2. `after_flush` walks `session.new` and captures insert rows from current column values — final generated PKs exist here.
3. `after_flush_postexec` writes all buffered rows (buffer lives in `session.info`, drained per flush — multi-flush transactions produce multiple batches) via ONE Core `session.execute(insert(core_audit_log), rows)` on the same connection — same transaction, so audit is exactly as atomic as the change, and event-handler writes are captured automatically because flush events fire for the shared session.

Columns are skipped per-model via `__audit_exclude__` (`password_hash` always; HR compensation is captured but the audit viewer masks it with the same `Masked` machinery).

**Context layer:** a pure-ASGI middleware creates `RequestContext` (request_id uuid, ip with trusted-proxy X-Forwarded-For handling, user_agent, method+path) in a ContextVar; `get_current_user` fills actor_user_id/tenant_id; the flush listeners read it (absent → actor NULL, source='system').

**Table `core_audit_log`:** id bigint identity, tenant_id NULLABLE, actor_user_id nullable, source (`'http'`|`'system'`), action (`'insert'`|`'update'`|`'delete'`), entity_table, entity_id text, diff JSON (JSONB via `with_variant`), request_id, ip, created_at; index (tenant_id, entity_table, entity_id, created_at). It does NOT carry `TenantMixin` (fix: `TenantMixin` implies NOT NULL + fail-closed filtering, which would break system-source rows and login-flow writes); the only read path is the admin audit endpoint whose service applies an explicit mandatory tenant predicate, covered by a dedicated cross-tenant leak test.

1	"""The universal journal: header + lines (D-017), the heart of Atlas finance.
2	
3	One append-only line table is the single source of truth for every FI/CO view (D-021); the
4	header carries entry-level lifecycle and the lines carry the postings plus every dimension a
5	statement projects from. Denormalized ``is_posted``/``posting_date``/``fiscal_period_id`` on the
6	line (set during the two-flush posting protocol) let projections query lines with NO header join
7	(D-021), which is why those columns live on the line at all.
8	
9	Money columns use ``MoneyType`` (D-015): exact NUMERIC on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on
10	SQLite, so the balance trigger's SUM and the one-side CHECK are exact on both engines. For v1,
11	functional amounts EQUAL transaction amounts (single functional currency, posting-time FX
12	translation lands in 4.3) — the columns exist now so the schema and triggers are FX-ready.
13	
14	Constraints declared here (rendered by migration 0009):
15	- ``ck_fin_journal_lines_one_side``: exactly one of debit/credit positive per line, the other
16	  zero — written on the stored columns so it holds on PG NUMERIC and SQLite micro-unit ints.
17	- the per-dialect TRIGGERS (period-open, balance, header immutability, line immutability) are
18	  NOT model constraints; they are hand-written DDL in the migration (D-017/D-018/D-022).
19	
20	Dimension columns (cost_center_id, profit_center_id, project_id, item_id, partner_id) are plain
21	``sa.Uuid`` WITHOUT FKs for now: the CO/project/inventory masters land in later PLAN phases
22	(4.7 controlling, 5 inventory, 11 projects); the ids are stored on the line today and FK'd when
23	those parent tables exist. partner_type + partner_id carry AP/AR open-item linkage (4.4+).
24	"""
25	
26	import uuid
27	from datetime import date, datetime
28	
29	import sqlalchemy as sa
30	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
31	
32	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
33	from app.core.models import (
34	    AuditMixin,
35	    Base,
36	    TenantMixin,
37	    TimestampMixin,
38	    UuidPKMixin,
39	    tenant_fk,
40	    tenant_unique,
41	)
42	from app.core.money import MoneyType
43	from app.modules.finance.constants import DocumentType, EntryStatus
44	
45	# Bare CHECK token (the D-022 ck convention wraps it as ck_<table>_<name>). Compares the STORED
46	# representation (NUMERIC on PG, micro-unit INTEGER on SQLite) so "> 0" / "= 0" hold on both.
47	_ONE_SIDE_CHECK = (
48	    "(transaction_debit_amount > 0 AND transaction_credit_amount = 0) "
49	    "OR (transaction_credit_amount > 0 AND transaction_debit_amount = 0)"
50	)
51	
52	
53	class JournalEntry(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
54	    """A journal-entry header (D-017). Registered in core_documents at creation (DocumentMixin)
55	    with doc_number NULL; the gapless ``entry_number`` is claimed at POSTING (D-012), so an
56	    abandoned draft burns no number — hence ``entry_number`` is NULLABLE with a partial unique
57	    index. An entry is single-transaction-currency (cross-currency events become multiple
58	    entries). ``reverses_entry_id`` points at the original an entry reverses;
59	    ``reversed_by_entry_id`` points at the reversing entry — both self composite tenant FKs.
60	    Audited (D-010): every financial mutation is auditable."""
61	
62	    __tablename__ = "fin_journal_entries"
63	    __table_args__ = (
64	        tenant_unique(),
65	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
66	        document_fk(),
67	        # Self composite tenant FKs: a reversal linkage can never cross tenants. Distinct
68	        # explicit names (the D-022 column-0 convention would collide on two self-FKs).
69	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
70	            ["tenant_id", "reverses_entry_id"],
71	            ["fin_journal_entries.tenant_id", "fin_journal_entries.id"],
72	            name="fk_fin_journal_entries_reverses_entry_id_fin_journal_entries",
73	        ),
74	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
75	            ["tenant_id", "reversed_by_entry_id"],
76	            ["fin_journal_entries.tenant_id", "fin_journal_entries.id"],
77	            name="fk_fin_journal_entries_reversed_by_entry_id_fin_journal_entries",
78	        ),
79	        # Composite tenant FK: the resolved period belongs to the same tenant.
80	        tenant_fk("fin_fiscal_periods", "fiscal_period_id"),
81	        # The gapless-number partial unique index is declared after the class (it needs the
82	        # column object for its dialect partial predicate, expressed without raw SQL so the
83	        # app/modules grep gate stays satisfied — see below).
84	    )
85	
86	    # NULL until posting (D-012 claim-at-permanence); the partial unique index above backstops it.
87	    entry_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
88	    posting_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
89	    # Resolved from posting_date at posting (D-018); nullable until then. The DB period trigger
90	    # re-derives by date so a wrong fiscal_period_id can never smuggle a posting into a closed
91	    # period.
92	    fiscal_period_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
93	    document_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
94	        sa.String(20), nullable=False, default=DocumentType.JOURNAL.value, server_default="JOURNAL"
95	    )
96	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
97	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
98	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
99	        sa.String(10), nullable=False, default=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value, server_default="DRAFT"
100	    )
101	    reverses_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
102	    reversed_by_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
103	    posted_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)
104	
105	
106	class JournalLine(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
107	    """A journal line (D-017): one posting on one account, one-sided (debit XOR credit). NOT
108	    AuditMixin — lines are written once with their immutable entry and never mutated after the
109	    posting flush, and the header's audit row records the entry-level change; auditing every
110	    line would double the trail with no extra signal (documented exclusion). The denormalized
111	    ``is_posted``/``posting_date``/``fiscal_period_id`` are set during the DRAFT->POSTED flush so
112	    statement projections read lines with no header join (D-021)."""
113	
114	    __tablename__ = "fin_journal_lines"
115	    __table_args__ = (
116	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
117	            "tenant_id",
118	            "journal_entry_id",
119	            "line_number",
120	            name="uq_fin_journal_lines_tenant_id_journal_entry_id_line_number",
121	        ),
122	        tenant_unique(),
123	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
124	        tenant_fk("fin_journal_entries", "journal_entry_id"),
125	        tenant_fk("fin_accounts", "account_id"),
126	        sa.CheckConstraint(_ONE_SIDE_CHECK, name="one_side"),
127	        # The statement-projection partial index is declared after the class (see below).
128	    )
129	
130	    journal_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
131	    line_number: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
132	    account_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
133	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
134	
135	    # Transaction-currency amounts (the entry's currency). Exactly one side is > 0 (one-side
136	    # CHECK). MoneyType: exact on both engines so the balance trigger's SUM is exact.
137	    transaction_debit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
138	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
139	    )
140	    transaction_credit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
141	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
142	    )
143	    # Functional-currency amounts. v1: equal to the transaction amounts (single functional
144	    # currency; posting-time FX translation in 4.3). The balance trigger SUM-checks THESE.
145	    functional_debit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
146	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
147	    )
148	    functional_credit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
149	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
150	    )
151	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
152	
153	    # Dimensions (all nullable; no FK yet — masters land in later phases, see module docstring).
154	    cost_center_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)

6	400-line cap, the finance models/ precedent). This file owns the 5.1 MASTER tables; the 5.2
7	warehouse/bin/move/quant STOCK tables live in ``models/stock.py``.
8	
9	Design decisions baked in here:
10	
11	- **Costing wiring on the category (D-020 + D-029).** ``ItemCategory`` carries the default
12	  costing method AND the three GL accounts COGS/valuation posting will need —
13	  ``inventory_account_id``, ``cogs_account_id``, ``price_difference_account_id`` — as OPAQUE
14	  ``sa.Uuid`` columns, NOT cross-module FKs (D-029): finance owns those accounts; the inventory
15	  service validates each id exists via ``finance/queries.py`` when set, and the journal-line
16	  precedent already stores finance dimension ids without an FK on a cross-module table. They are
17	  NULLABLE on the category (a SERVICE-only category needs none); a STOCKED item's category must
18	  carry them before that item can post moves — validated when moves land (5.2+), not in 5.1.
19	
20	- **costing_method on the item (D-020).** Defaulted from the category at create but STORED on the
21	  item, because the item is the costing unit and D-020 lets it change only while no stock exists.
22	
23	- **UoM convention (the chosen one of the two the task offered): per-item BASE + ALTERNATES.**
24	  Each item has ONE ``base_uom_id``; quantities are stored/costed in the base UoM. An
25	  ``UomConversion`` row expresses an ALTERNATE UoM for that item as ``factor_to_base`` —
26	  multiplying a quantity in the alternate UoM by the factor yields the base-UoM quantity (an
27	  item whose base is EA and has BOX with factor 12 means 1 BOX = 12 EA). ``UNIQUE(tenant_id,
28	  item_id, alt_uom_id)`` — one factor per (item, alternate). This is the standard ERP shape
29	  (S/4HANA's alternative-UoM table): simpler than a full from/to graph, and base<->alt and
30	  alt<->alt conversions all derive from the single per-alternate factor (service.convert_quantity).

32	- **Lot / SerialNumber are MASTER tables only for 5.1.** They are defined so the schema is
33	  receipt-ready, but instances are CREATED during receipts (5.2+); 5.1 ships no CRUD for them.

36	referenced by a child, ``tenant_fk()`` composites for every cross-row link so a child can never

1	"""Sales quote → order documents (PLAN 7.2): ``Quote`` + ``QuoteLine`` and ``SalesOrder`` +
2	``SalesOrderLine`` — the O2C spine, mirrored on the procurement requisition/PO shape.
3	
4	A quote is the pre-sales document (a price offer); an order is the committing O2C document (a
5	customer commitment ≈ a purchase order, mirrored). Each header mixes in ``DocumentMixin``
6	(registered in core_documents) and carries a gapless number claimed AT CREATION (D-012/D-040 — a
7	quote/order is referenceable the moment it exists, the procurement-document precedent, NOT finance's
8	number-at-post branch). ``total_amount`` is the maintained sum of line nets.
9	
10	Order specifics:
11	
12	- ``customer_id`` is a composite tenant FK to ``sales_customers`` (intra-module, so a real FK — the
13	  customer master is sales-owned). ``payment_terms_days`` is SNAPSHOT from the customer at creation
14	  (so a later customer edit cannot rewrite an open order's terms — the 7.4 invoice reads the
15	  snapshot, the PO precedent).
16	- ``source_quote_id`` (nullable composite tenant FK) links an order back to the ACCEPTED quote it
17	  was converted from (+ the docflow edge).
18	- ``credit_check_status`` (nullable) records the confirm-time credit result
19	(PASSED/BLOCKED/RELEASED,
20	  D-044).
21	
22	Line specifics carry an OPAQUE inventory ``item_id`` / ``uom_id`` (D-029, plain ``sa.Uuid``,
23	validated via inventory/queries, never a cross-module FK), the resolved/overridable ``unit_price``,
24	an optional per-line discount (type + value), the derived ``line_amount`` (qty × unit_price −
25	discount), ``delivered_quantity`` (raised by 7.3), ``invoiced_quantity`` (raised by 7.4), and an
26	opaque finance ``tax_code_id`` (nullable — the 7.4 invoice uses it). Money/quantity use
27	``MoneyType`` / ``QuantityType`` (D-015, exact on both engines).
28	
29	Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value; the service
30	maps to/from the constants classes. Every table follows the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop
31	(``tenant_unique()`` + ``tenant_fk()`` composites + ``document_fk()`` on the headers).

1	"""HR org masters (PLAN 10.1, parity HCM core = employees + departments + positions + org chart):
2	the ``Department``, ``Position`` and ``Employee`` masters.
3	
4	THREE tables, one concern (the HCM org core). The hr models became a PACKAGE in PLAN 10.2 (leave
5	landed in a sibling ``leave.py``); this file holds the org masters unchanged.
6	
7	All three are MASTERS keyed by a USER-SUPPLIED ``code`` unique per tenant (the item-code / work-
8	centre precedent — no gapless document number, no DocumentMixin: HR masters are not posted documents
9	in the D-012 sense).
10	
11	THE DEPARTMENT↔MANAGER CIRCULAR REFERENCE (D-052). A department has a manager EMPLOYEE; an employee
12	belongs to a department — a hard composite FK each way would be a circular table dependency the
13	migration could not order. Resolution: ``Department.manager_employee_id`` is a PLAIN nullable
14	``sa.Uuid`` (opaque, validated in the service against ``hr_employees``), NOT a composite FK; the
15	employee→department side IS a real composite FK. So the dependency is one-directional at the DDL
16	level (employee → department), and the manager link is a service-validated soft reference. The
17	EMPLOYEE's org-chart reporting line (``manager_id``) and the DEPARTMENT hierarchy (``parent_id``)
18	are intra-table SELF composite FKs (a child can never point at a parent of another tenant); the
19	service
20	guards both against cycles with a bounded walk-up.
21	
22	CROSS-MODULE / SOFT IDS ARE OPAQUE (D-029/§5). ``Department.cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance
23	cost-centre id (nullable, validated via finance/queries when set — never a cross-module FK).
24	``Employee.user_id`` is an OPAQUE core users id (nullable, validated via a core user probe when
25	set — an employee MAY also be a system user; never a hard FK from a module table to core_users).
26	
27	THE MASKED FIELDS (D-009/D-052) live on ``Employee`` as ordinary columns — ``base_salary``
28	(MoneyType), ``currency_code``, ``national_id``, ``tax_id``, ``date_of_birth``, ``bank_account``.
29	The
30	masking is a READ-side concern of the schema layer (the ``Masked`` serializer), not the model; the
31	columns store the real values. They are excluded from the audit diff (D-010) — compensation/PII is
32	captured in v1 only through the same masking machinery in the audit viewer (a documented later); for
33	now ``__audit_exclude__`` keeps the raw values out of the diff rows entirely, matching the
34	password_hash precedent on User.
35	"""
